correctness.rationale: The support classification follows directly from complete-multipartite adjacency. A set meeting at least three parts is secure because replacing one defender can remove at most one occupied part and leaves at least two. For support \(\{i,j\}\), an omitted vertex in part \(i\) can be defended from part \(j\); if only one vertex of \(j\) is selected, the exchange remains dominating exactly when it fills part \(i\), giving \(t_i\le1\) or \(s_j\ge2\), and symmetrically for \(j\). A one-part dominating set must equal that whole part, and security is exactly the stated singleton exception. The polynomial is the disjoint support count with inclusion-exclusion over the two one-defender obstructions. A fresh direct brute-force replay on representative part profiles through order five matched the criterion for every subset; the unrestricted theorem rests on the symbolic argument.
residual_risks: The theorem is specific to ordinary secure domination on complete multipartite graphs.
